observations.content: User's first Aptis attempt was 20/07/2024: Listening 48 (C), Reading 44 (C), Writing 46 (C), Speaking 36 (B1), Grammar & Vocab 40 (no CEFR shown), overall C, total 174; user said that result involved luck and long prep time, and now they have much less time.
Assistant identified Speaking 36/B1 as clear weak spot (10+ points below other C skills) and G/V 40 as second, the highest-leverage targets.
User selected 'Other' for exam-timing question: 'mình còn khoảng 1 tuần ôn tập, mục tiêu B2 nãy mình quên gửi' — only about 1 week of prep time left and target is B2.
User selected 'Chỉ Overall B2' (option 2) for B2 requirement question — only needs Overall B2, not B2 per skill.
Current probing showed user gaps at B2/C1 grammar including wrong mixed conditional, unknown inversion, and unknown 'obscure' vocab word.

Assistant's first paseo_get_agent_activity call failed with MCP error -32602 (expected agentId string, got undefined because assistant sent 'agent_id'); retried with correct 'agentId' parameter and succeeded.

Researcher completed an Aptis ESOL General reference brief from primary British Council sources; key finding: overall CEFR = rounded average of the four skill CEFR levels, NOT the total score, and overall numeric score is a separate sum /200, calculated independently.
Researcher: times. The total session ~3 hours with no breaks.
Researcher: Core (Grammar & Vocabulary) gets a 0-50 scale score but NO CEFR level; Core acts as tie-breaker when a skill score falls in the grey area just below a cut score.
Researcher official revised-2020 cut scores (starting point of each level): Listening A1 8/A2 16/B1 24/B2 34/C 42; Reading 8/16/26/38/46; Writing 6/18/26/40/48; Speaking 4/16/26/41/48.
Aptis General/Teachers/Teens cannot differentiate C1 from C2 — anything above B2 reported as 'C'; only Aptis Advanced differentiates C1/C2.

With updated cut scores user's Speaking 36 is firmly B1 (B2 starts at 41); Reading 44 and Listening 48 and Writing 46 are C, so user is in decent shape for overall B2 since requirement is only overall.

Researcher corrected user's assumptions: Reading Part 4 is heading-matching on a ~750-word text, not narrative gap-fill; Listening is 28±4 questions (25 is legacy pre-2020); BC prepare page mislabels Speaking Part 1 as 'Sentence comprehension' (actual: 'Personal information').

Researcher noted there is no official published Aptis vocabulary list; BC directs candidates to BC/EAQUALS Core Inventory and LearnEnglish; the ~1000-word 'Aptis vocab lists' circulating in Vietnam are unofficial community documents.

Vietnam pitfalls flagged by researcher: Writing Part 4 register collapse caps at B1; describing the photo in Speaking Part 4 instead of answering abstract questions caps score; P2 word-limit overruns; memorised scripts score 0; stale pre-2020 cut scores circulated by VN prep sites; old CMND invalid from 01/01/2025 (passport or new CCCD only); registration only via distributor aptistests.vn; certificates from unauthorized channels not accepted (fraud alert).
